lines: If your AI's tools take a user ID as an argument, you've already written the bug.
The model fills in every argument. So one wrong guess, or one hostile request, can point that tool at someone else's data.
This isn't hypothetical. In 2025, Asana took its AI connector offline for nearly two weeks after finding a bug that could expose data to other organizations.
The fix is to take the field away. Who's asking comes from the session, not the arguments. Send a request naming someone else's account, and the server writes to yours anyway. Theirs isn't touched.
One real memory tool works this way. Six fields, all required, and the conversation ID isn't one of them. Its description tells the model why: the server derives it.
Let the model choose what. Let the server decide whose.
facts: Script v4 (Robin, 2026-10-30: the channel is for people developing with AI; no abstract concepts nobody will deal with). Framed as a builder's rule: no identity or scope fields in a tool's input schema. I-II: where-logic-lives, rules must hold 'if a prompt is missed, the model is confused, or the caller is hostile'; 'the caller could not send a source-turn identifier and independently pair it with an arbitrary chat_id'; mcp-tool-design, a model has 'decent reason to think' chat_id belongs in write_memory. III: stakes only, NOT a claim about Asana's cause (Asana has not stated one). BleepingComputer and The Register, 2025-06-18: launched May 1, found June 4, offline June 5 to 17; Asana to customers: 'this bug could have potentially exposed certain information from your Asana domain to other Asana MCP users.' IV: systems repo storage-routing test (S12): identity and routing come 'from the authenticated context and from nothing a caller supplies'; a payload naming workspace B 'lands its write in workspace A (the context's) and leaves B unchanged'. V: mcp-tool-design: write_memory 'declares six properties and requires all six. chat_id is not among them'; its description: 'chat_id is NOT an input, it is derived server-side from source_turn_id.' VI: where-logic-lives: 'Let the model choose among safe actions. Reject unsafe states at a boundary the model cannot waive.' YouTube description cites the two news articles and the two devweb articles. Earlier scripts in vo/audition/.
